findings.public_spec: Positive-edge D flip-flop with XOR feedback and no reset; no initial value is specified.
findings.observed: Candidate has no initialization. The RTL testbench terminates at 101 ns with NETLIST_INITIAL_STATE_UNKNOWN, before any completion record. The known-initial-state requirement comes from the hardware oracle reused for RTL simulation.
findings.interpretation: This does not establish a functional RTL error against the public circuit description. The synthesized candidate was not evaluated because the RTL stage stopped. Keep it as an evaluator-policy limitation, not a confirmed model failure.
findings.statistical_treatment: Retain the frozen raw result; disclose separately. Any exclusion beyond the two predeclared specification conflicts is post-hoc sensitivity analysis, never a silently revised primary score.

findings.method: Host-only static comparison of the unchanged public buggy example, approved eight-bit output interpretation, reference source, and recorded model revisions. No new reference information is sent to the model.
findings.public_example: The expression (~sel & a) | (sel & b) points to a for sel=0 and b for sel=1 when fixing its width/mask bug as an eight-bit mux.
findings.observed: The initial candidate receives 220 mismatches in 226 checks. A recorded repair reverses selection to match the hidden reference; its comment still describes the original polarity.
findings.approved_erratum_scope: The user approved an eight-bit output. That approval does not authorize changing select polarity or treating the hidden reference as the public specification.
findings.interpretation: A reference-matching repair here is not established as a public-specification improvement. This is an additional validity finding, not part of the two predeclared conflict exclusions.
findings.statistical_treatment: Retain original scores and report separately; any exclusion is explicitly post-hoc sensitivity analysis.
